propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Praesta, quaesumus, omnipotens Deus: ut, qui paschalia festa peregimus,
haec, te largiente, moribus et vita teneamus. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum
Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

provenance.locator: editorial-projection artifact physical lines 25-27; antecedent printed p. 281; text-layer lines 43796-43801, heading 'Secreta.' at 43795
provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: THE 1862 TEXT LAYER READS 'et qui causam' WHERE THE 1962 READS 'et, cui causam'. This is a word, not a point.; 1862 'exultantis' for the 1962 'exsultantis'; 1862 sets no comma after 'et'; 1862 conclusion is the short cue 'Per Dominum.'. Corroboration: Venice 1570 at text-layer lines 43962-43965, whose line 43964 reads 'cut cauſaʒ táti audi) paeſtititti' = 'cui causam tanti gaudii praestitisti'. The Vatican typica 1604 could NOT be used: its Dominica in albis leaf is missing or unreadable in that scan's OCR (searches on 'Quasi modo', 'geniti', 'munera' and 'gaudii' over the whole file return nothing in that stretch).. Recorded limitation: THIS IS THE WEAKEST ENTRY IN THE LANE AND THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO BE WRONG. 'qui' is a real Latin word and reads plausibly, so I cannot tell from the text layer alone whether the 1862 Pustet genuinely prints 'qui' or whether the recogniser turned a 'c' into a 'q'. Against the OCR-error reading: 'cu' is recognised correctly elsewhere on the same leaves (cujus at 43904, 43981, 44009). For it: this scan's pointing is already garbled here ('qusesumus^' at 43797 for 'quaesumus,'). The prayer as a whole is corroborated word for word in the 1862; the disputed relative pronoun is carried by the 1570, not by the 1862. If the reviewer requires that the 1862 alone carry every word of a matched entry, this one does not qualify and should be held for an 1862 page-image check.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Quaesumus, Domine Deus noster: ut sacrosancta mysteria, quae pro
reparationis nostrae munimine contulisti: et praesens nobis remedium esse
facias, et futurum. Per Dominum.
